unit.title: JavaScript: lists and loops
unit.description: Arrays, positions counted from 0, length, push, repeating code with for and for...of

cards.definition: An ordered list of values between square brackets, separated by commas.
The position of an item in a list, counted from 0: the first item is at position 0.
Adds one or more items at the end of a list, and changes that list.
cards.example: colors.push("pink") makes the list one item longer.

cards.definition: Repeats a block a set number of times, with a counter that changes at each turn.
cards.example: for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) runs 3 times, with i at 0, 1, then 2.

cards.definition: Goes through the items of a list one by one and gives each item in turn to the block.
cards.example: for (const c of colors) { console.log(c); } prints each color.

cards.definition: Adds 1 to a variable that holds a number: i++ is short for i = i + 1.

exercises.explain: Positions (indexes) start at 0: fruits[0] is the first item, fruits[1] the second one.
whyWrong: pear is at position 1: counting starts at 0.
kiwi is at position 2, the last one.
Position 0 exists: it is the first item.

exercises.explain: .length gives how many items the list holds. The last index is always length minus 1.
whyWrong: length counts the items from 1; only indexes start at 0.
There are three items, no more.
length gives a number, not the last item.

exercises.prompt: What does the list contain after these lines?
exercises.explain: push() adds an item at the END of the list, and changes the list itself.
whyWrong: push adds at the end of the list, not at the start.
push adds an item; it does not replace the list.
push changes the list: "hat" is now in it.

exercises.prompt: How many times is Hi printed?
exercises.explain: i starts at 0, the loop runs while i < 3, and i++ adds 1 after each turn: 0, 1, 2. Three turns.
whyWrong: i takes the values 0, 1 and 2: that makes three turns.
The loop stops when i reaches 3, before a fourth turn.
The block runs at every turn of the loop, not once.

exercises.explain: The counter starts at 1 and the loop runs while i <= 3, so i takes 1, 2, then 3.
whyWrong: i starts at 1 here, not at 0.
<= includes 3: the loop also runs when i is 3.
console.log is inside the loop: it runs at every turn.

exercises.explain: for...of hands each item of the list to the block in turn: first "red", then "blue".
whyWrong: The loop goes through every item, not just the first.
for...of gives the items themselves, not their positions.
c takes each value of the list in turn.

exercises.prompt: In ["a", "b", "c"], the item "c" is at index 3.
exercises.explain: Counting starts at 0: "a" is at 0, "b" at 1 and "c" at 2.

exercises.prompt: Build a line that adds "milk" at the end of the list shopping.
exercises.explain: shopping.push("milk") adds the item at the end of the list.

exercises.prompt: This loop should print the three names, but it skips Ana and ends with undefined. Which line is wrong?
exercises.explain: Indexes go from 0 to length minus 1. Start at 0 and stop before length: for (let i = 0; i < names.length; i++).
The loop adds each price to total: 0 + 5, then + 10, then + 15. A classic way to add up a list.
whyWrong: 15 is only the last price; the loop adds all three.
The prices are numbers, so + adds them.
total changes at every turn of the loop.
